label: prf:frobenius-pairing-exists
title: Proof of existence of the Frobenius pairing
html:
The pairing in question is attached to the Frobenius object A: its value is the composite \int_A \circ \mu, and its non-degeneracy is the invertibility of the induced adjoint A \to A^\vee.

Existence is immediate: \mu and \int_A are part of the quantum- universe data, so the composite \int_A \circ \mu is a morphism in \mathbf{C} by composition.

Non-degeneracy is where the provenance matters. A quantum universe is not rigid — \mathbf{C} carries no duality functor, so there is no ambient A^\vee to map into and no ambient snake identities to invoke. What plays that role is supplied by axiom 2 on A alone: the Frobenius–Hopf structure carries a coevaluation \tilde\eta \colon \mathbf{1} \to A \otimes A together with the two snake identities for the pairing \mathrm{ev} = \int_A \circ\, \mu. Those identities exhibit A as its own dual; they are not consequences of a rigid structure on \mathbf{C}, and asserting them is exactly what axiom 2 does.

The pairing is therefore non-degenerate because the Frobenius–Hopf data says so, and the self-duality A \cong A^\vee is a conclusion about A rather than an instance of a duality every object enjoys. Rigidity is imposed one level up, on a quantum observable universe.
